title: Incremental Embeddings Update Protocol (scratchpad)
content:
Goal:
- Define a simple, robust protocol for incremental updates to embeddings indexes used by Redwood-hosted and on-device feature stores.
- Support low-latency local updates (e.g., user-level personalization) while keeping central index reasonably consistent for search/semantic-match.
- Minimize network overhead and storage bloat with compact deltas and pruning rules.

Motivating scenarios:
1) Per-user private vectors updated on-device (note additions, short-term history). Server receives periodic checkpoints, merges into shared index.
2) High-velocity annotation stream (enterprise customer) submits label+text; embeddings pipeline generates vectors and wants to push only changed/added vectors to Dedicated clusters.
3) Model re-embedding (model upgrade) where many vectors need to be re-indexed later without duplicating entire index during rollout.

Design constraints / non-goals:
- Not trying to be a full CRDT solution; eventual consistency with well-defined conflict resolution is OK.
- Heavyweight distributed transaction semantics are out of scope.
- Privacy: per-user vectors may be encrypted client-side; protocol should avoid leaking content in diffs.

Core concepts:
- Document ID (doc_id): stable external id (string) assigned by producer.
- Vector ID (vec_id): unique id for a vector instance (string), usually composed of doc_id + version nonce.
- Epoch (int string): monotonically increasing per-producer counter for strong ordering of updates from that producer.
- Delta bundle: gzipped JSONL blob containing a list of operations (insert/update/delete) with minimal metadata.
- Checkpoint manifest: small JSON listing vector counts, last epoch, checksum, and compaction hint.

Wire API (HTTP/REST sketch)
- POST /v1/embeddings/delta
  - Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>, X-Producer: <producer-id>, X-Epoch: <epoch>
  - Body: multipart/form-data or application/octet-stream. Fields: manifest.json, delta_blob.gz (binary)
  - Response: 200 {"accepted": true, "server_epoch": 2345, "assigned_shard": "ded-03"}

- GET /v1/embeddings/checkpoint?producer=<id>&epoch=<n>
  - Return: latest manifest for producer, helpful for resume/reconcile.

Delta bundle JSONL ops (line-per-op):
- insert: {"op":"insert","doc_id":"...","vec_id":"...","epoch":"123","embedding":<base64|quantized-b64>,"meta":{...}}
- update: {"op":"update","vec_id":"...","epoch":"124","embedding":<...>,"meta":{...}}
- delete: {"op":"delete","vec_id":"...","epoch":"125"} 

Important notes on payloads:
- Embedding payload: best-effort compression. Two representations allowed: raw float32 base64 OR quantized int8 packed base64 with metadata giving scale/zero. Server should accept both.
- Optionally support a sidecar index diff format for extremely large batches: refs to blob ids already uploaded to object store.

Ordering & idempotency
- Every producer must monotonically increase Epoch. Server will reject bundles with epoch <= last_seen_epoch for that producer (unless explicit force flag).
- Each vec_id is unique and can be upserted; server stores last-write-wins by (producer, epoch, vec_id). If same vec_id appears with lower epoch, it's ignored.
- For cross-producer collisions (two producers generate same vec_id), server falls back to (producer_id, vec_id) namespace. Recommend vec_id include producer prefix.

Consistency model and visibility
- Nearline ingestion: delta bundles are accepted quickly but may be visible to search after a short ingestion window (e.g., 1–5s) during indexing and sharding.
- Stronger: optionally support sync commit mode: POST with ?commit=sync which blocks until vector visible (suitable for tests/critical updates).

Batching & performance knobs
- Producers: should pack small writes into bundles to amortize overhead. Recommend 256–8192 vectors per bundle depending on vector size.
- Server: accept small bundles but maintain mempool. Background compaction merges per-producer segments to reduce fragmentation.

Compaction and garbage collection
- Each producer is allowed to submit tombstones (delete ops). Tombstones carry a TTL indicating when coarse GC can permanently remove vector bytes. Default TTL = 30d (configurable).
- Compaction runs per-shard and merges in-disk segments older than X epochs or when tombstone density > Y.

Model re-embedding strategy
- Don't require reindex of other producers immediately. Provide two-phase update: 1) producers generate re-embedding bundles with mapping old_vec_id -> new_vec_id (or doc_id mapping). 2) Server supports migrate op: {"op":"migrate","old_vec_id":"...","new_vec_id":"...","epoch":"..."}
- During migration, queries should consult overlay map that links old to new until compaction removes old entries.

Failure modes & recovery
- Duped bundles: server dedup by checksum+producer+epoch.
- Partial apply (process crash mid-bundle): bundles are atomic at service layer; either all ops applied or none (transactional per-bundle).
- Producer crash mid-epoch: producer replays last unacknowledged epoch with same epoch number and a stable bundle id; server must accept replayed bundle idempotently.

On-device considerations
- Small devices should prefer producing compact quantized deltas and only send diffs when on WiFi or on user-driven sync.
- Sensitive vectors can be E2E encrypted; server will store but won't be able to read content for re-embedding later. For re-embedding, device must replay plaintext if allowed.

ASCII flow (simple):
Client (producer) --(delta bundle)-> Ingest API --write to--> Mempool --> Indexer workers --> Shard store
                 
Manifest exchange:
Client: POST chunk -> Server returns assigned_shard + receipt_id -> Client updates local manifest with receipt_id.

Open questions / TODO:
- Should we version the delta schema (v1, v2) or include a schema field per bundle? (lean v1 + semver)
- Backpressure signals: how to expose mempool pressure to producers? (HTTP 429 + Retry-After; or websocket push)
- Exactly-how to handle encrypted vectors during model refresh (decryption required or device replay?)
- Embedding representation: do we support FP16 as wire format? (size vs fidelity tradeoffs)
- Add a small streaming variant over gRPC for low-latency single-vector updates.

Immediate next steps (personal checklist):
- Draft proto definitions for ops and manifest (proto v3 sketch).
- Spike: implement small ingest shim that accepts gzipped JSONL bundles and simulates apply in memory (Samir taking this).
- Perf numbers: measure bundle sizes for 512-d float32 vs int8 quantized for typical user data.
- Draft SDK helpers (python/js) to build bundles and handle retries.

Notes to self:
- Keep protocol minimal; prefer orthogonality to our existing inference HTTP APIs.
- Add example error codes mapping in a follow-up doc.

Unresolved:
- Locking/ordering semantics for cross-producer re-embedding migrations (race conditions).
- How this plays with Dedicated vs Hosted topologies (routing of per-producer data to tenant-specific shards).

References / scratch links:
- JIRA: INF-482 (embeddings incremental ingestion epic)
- Git PR: github.com/redwood/embeddings-sync-proto/pull/7
- Slack: #embeddings-sync thread (link placeholder)

End of scratchpad.
